short.title: Alexandria's Royal Tomb Found Under City #Shorts
short.title_plain: Alexandria's Royal Tomb Found Under City
short.hook: A 2,000-year-old royal tomb in Alexandria may be the Ptolemaic Sema.
script: A 2,000-year-old royal tomb in Alexandria may be the Ptolemaic Sema.
Its square foundations are slightly larger than the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus.
A tunnel discovery revealed hidden walls and new dimensions.
Archaeologists link its location and walls to the known Sema tomb.
The structure dates to Ptolemy IV’s reign, 245–204 BC.
Further excavation is needed to confirm its royal identity.
Could this be the royal mausoleum, or just a grand tomb?
Tap the link below for the full case file.
short.description:
A structure in Alexandria’s Royal Quarter may be the Ptolemaic royal tomb known as the Sema. Its square foundations are larger than the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus, and a recently discovered underground tunnel helped identify hidden walls. Researchers link the site’s location and walls to the known Sema, but further excavation is needed to confirm the identification. Source: eKathimerini.com, https://www.ekathimerini.com/culture/1322488/greek-archaeologists-close-in-on-ptolemaic-royal-tomb/
